#109\\u0027s audit of \\u0060NodeBootstrap.EnsureAsync\\u0060 was wrong, which retracts #109\\u0027s elimination of its own hypothesis (2), the gap the audit missed was real, and the guard #109 shipped has since gained a marker it never described** (2026-09-01, independent pre-PR review of the same branch, cycle 1). #109 concluded \\u0060EnsureAsync\\u0060 \\u0022is called only from CLI command handlers and \\u0060NodeContext\\u0060, never directly from a test\\u0022 \\u2014 true only of *direct* calls: \\u0060NodeContext.InitializeAsync\\u0060 (\\u0060src/Hall9k.Daemon/NodeContext.cs\\u0060) calls it, and fourteen integration test classes across forty-six call sites (\\u0060DispatchEngineTests\\u0060, \\u0060LeaseLivenessTests\\u0060, \\u0060CardPublicationEngineTests\\u0060, \\u0060TaskProjectionBackfillTests\\u0060, \\u0060ReviewEngineTests\\u0060, \\u0060TaskDispatchGuardTests\\u0060, \\u0060RunSupervisorTests\\u0060, \\u0060ReviewResolveCommandTests\\u0060, \\u0060CloseoutEngineTests\\u0060, \\u0060RunLauncherTests\\u0060, \\u0060JiraWriteRetryEngineTests\\u0060, \\u0060DispatchCeilingTests\\u0060, \\u0060TokenBudgetRetryEngineTests\\u0060, \\u0060PrReviewEngineTests\\u0060) call \\u0060InitializeAsync\\u0060 directly against a fresh \\u0060PostgresFixture\\u0060 database that carries no \\u0060ConnectionDetails\\u0060 row yet, so \\u0060EnsureAsync\\u0060 fell through to \\u0060GhLogin()\\u0060 and shelled to the real \\u0060gh\\u0060 on every one of those tests\\u0027 first run \\u2014 confirmed on this machine by pointing an instrumented fake \\u0060gh\\u0060 at \\u0060PATH\\u0060 before the fix below and observing it invoked, then re-confirming it silent after. That observation retracts half of #109\\u0027s own conclusion, and not just its audit: #109\\u0027s hypothesis (2), \\u0022a test shelling to the real \\u0060gh\\u0060\\u0022, was not eliminated, it held. \\u0060NodeBootstrap.GhLogin\\u0060 has shelled out whenever \\u0060EnsureAsync\\u0060 finds no GitHub connection since \\u006076b97ebd\\u0060 (2026-08-16), so that behavior was live in the tree on 2026-08-29, and #109\\u0027s headline claim of \\u0022a real network call eliminated by direct evidence\\u0022 and its flat \\u0022Neither hypothesis holds.\\u0022 are both false as written; a reader working through \\u00A716 in order should take this sentence as superseding them. What the retraction does not do is make the \\u0060gh\\u0060 call the abort\\u0027s cause. \\u0060NodeBootstrap.RunQuick\\u0060 reads the child\\u0027s stdout to EOF with \\u0060ReadToEnd()\\u0060 before it ever calls \\u0060WaitForExit(3000)\\u0060, so that call is not the bound it reads as: the wall-clock cost is the child\\u0027s full runtime, ordinarily sub-second, and the 3000 ms cap only covers whatever remains after stdout closes. The whole cost of the missed gap was therefore one un-hard-bounded \\u0060gh api user\\u0060 per fresh fixture database (the connection it registers is durable, so later tests against the same database never re-ran it): a slow first test, with nothing on that path that terminates the host, which is a poor fit for a VSTest-level \\u0022Test Run Aborted: Test host process crashed\\u0022. #109\\u0027s hypothesis (1), the grep for a process-terminating call, does still hold and is what rules the termination shape out. The consequence for #109\\u0027s conclusion is therefore narrower than a reversal but real: that entry reached decision #108\\u0027s unbounded-container OOM by exhaustion over two eliminated hypotheses, and only one of the two is actually eliminated, so the OOM is the best-supported explanation the timeline carries rather than the only surviving one. The scar is the same shape #109 itself already named for the grep-built enumeration two paragraphs earlier in that entry: an exhaustiveness claim followed direct callers and stopped at \\u0060NodeContext\\u0060 instead of asking who constructs and initializes one. Closing it does not get the \\u0060ProcessRunner\\u0060 seam #109 left as an out-of-scope gap for \\u0060NodeBootstrap\\u0060, \\u0060PullRequestOpener\\u0060, and \\u0060GitHubPullRequestInspector\\u0060 alike \\u2014 threading one through \\u0060EnsureAsync\\u0060 would force a signature change onto every one of its roughly thirty production call sites across \\u0060Hall9k.Cli\\u0060\\u0027s command handlers for a seam only tests would ever use. Instead, \\u0060tests/Hall9k.Tests/Fakes/NodeBootstrapSeed.cs\\u0060 registers a GitHub \\u0060ConnectionDetails\\u0060 through the real \\u0060ConnectionAggregate\\u0060 event stream (\\u0060ConnectionDecider.Register\\u0060, the same construction \\u0060NodeBootstrap\\u0060 itself uses, following \\u0060TaskSeed\\u0060\\u0027s own precedent of seeding through deciders rather than writing documents directly) before calling \\u0060InitializeAsync\\u0060, so \\u0060EnsureAsync\\u0060\\u0027s \\u0060connection is null\\u0060 check is false and \\u0060GhLogin\\u0060 is never reached; forty-five of the forty-six call sites now go through \\u0060NodeBootstrapSeed.NewNodeAsync\\u0060 instead of constructing an uninitialized \\u0060NodeContext\\u0060 and calling \\u0060InitializeAsync\\u0060 directly. The forty-sixth, \\u0060The_loop_waits_for_this_node_to_have_an_identity_before_its_first_sweep\\u0060 (then in \\u0060CardPublicationEngineTests\\u0060, folded into \\u0060RenderSweepTests\\u0060 on 2026-09-08 by the test-suite runtime task), deliberately keeps its own direct \\u0060new NodeContext()\\u0060 and a deferred \\u0060InitializeAsync\\u0060 call \\u2014 the test exists to exercise the loop\\u0027s pre-bootstrap window, so the initialization has to happen on its own schedule rather than bundled inside \\u0060NewNodeAsync\\u0060 \\u2014 and is made gh-safe instead by calling \\u0060NodeBootstrapSeed.SeedGitHubConnectionAsync\\u0060 explicitly, immediately before it. \\u0060PullRequestOpener\\u0060 and \\u0060GitHubPullRequestInspector\\u0060 were correctly audited as unreached and this correction does not touch them. Separately, the one direct check #109 named as available but unperformed \\u2014 a macOS jetsam log for 2026-08-29 \\u2014 was run in this pass: \\u0060/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/\\u0060 retains entries back to 2026-08-25 and does write \\u0060JetsamEvent-*\\u0060 reports (one exists for 2026-09-01), but none exists for 2026-08-29, which neither confirms decision #108\\u0027s OOM-kill mechanism nor rules it out \\u2014 #109 already noted the same pressure events on 2026-08-23/08-24 could equally have been Brian killing processes by hand, which also leaves no jetsam report \\u2014 so the 2026-08-29 abort\\u0027s mechanism stays exactly as unconfirmed as #109 recorded it, now with the one reachable check actually run rather than left open, and (per the retraction above) resting on one eliminated hypothesis rather than the two #109 counted. Finally, #109 described the guard as naming \\u0022only those two literal spellings\\u0022 (\\u0060Environment.Exit\\u0060/\\u0060Environment.FailFast\\u0060) and listed \\u0060Process.GetCurrentProcess().Kill()\\u0060 among what \\u0022is not caught\\u0022 \\u2014 a later commit on this same branch added a third marker, \\u0060GetCurrentProcess().Kill\\u0060, which #109\\u0027s text was never updated to reflect. That marker still cannot reach the two call sites its own doc comment named as justification (\\u0060SingleInstanceGuard\\u0060, \\u0060WindowsStopRequestWatcher\\u0060): both bind \\u0060Process.GetCurrentProcess()\\u0060 to a local (\\u0060using Process current = ...\\u0060) before any read, so an added \\u0060.Kill()\\u0060 there reads \\u0060current.Kill()\\u0060, which the literal marker never matches \\u2014 \\u0060ProcessTerminationGuardTests\\u0060\\u0027 own doc comment and its positive-control assertion message now say so as a stated limit instead of claiming coverage they do not have. The guard\\u0027s scan also now covers \\u0060tests/\\u0060 alongside \\u0060src/\\u0060, closing the one scope gap #109 flagged as real but left undefended (\\u0022this scope limit is not otherwise guarded against\\u0022), since a termination call added directly to a fixture or fake is exactly as reachable from a test as one added to production code. The seed-helper rule this entry describes is itself enforced rather than left a convention, the same way decision #108\\u0027s container rule rests on \\u0060ContainerRoutingGuardTests\\u0060: \\u0060NodeBootstrapConventionGuardTests\\u0060 (\\u0060tests/Hall9k.Tests/Domain/\\u0060) scans comment/string-stripped source across the whole \\u0060tests/\\u0060 directory and fails the build for any file constructing a \\u0060NodeContext\\u0060 directly, so the forty-sixth call site does not have to be caught by a reviewer. Two files are exempt by repository-relative path, both file-wide rather than case-specific: \\u0060NodeBootstrapSeed.cs\\u0060, where the one legitimate construction lives, and \\u0060RenderSweepTests.cs\\u0060 (\\u0060CardPublicationEngineTests.cs\\u0060 until 2026-09-08), whose deliberate deferred-initialization case is described above \\u2014 a second direct construction added elsewhere in that file is not caught. Like both sibling guards, it documents its own blind spot in its doc comment: the marker names \\u0060new NodeContext()\\u0060 and \\u0060NodeContext name = new()\\u0060, so a nullable-annotated declaration (\\u0060NodeContext? node = new();\\u0060) and a return-position construction (\\u0060private static NodeContext Node() =\\u003E new();\\u0060) both escape it. **Does this block the later vision?** No: a test-only seed helper, a new test-tree-local guard, a guard doc correction, and a guard scope widening \\u2014 no production behavior change, no domain or event-model is configured in the operator\\u0027s own units at two levels: the node ceiling is task runs, and a second knob caps agent sessions within one run** (2026-08-30, origin: diagnosed live on 2026-08-30 \\u2014 the node ceiling was denominated in agent sessions (\\u0060maxConcurrentAgentSessions\\u0060), but a run reserved its peak of 2 sessions at admission for its whole life, so the setting had dead values: 3 admitted exactly what 2 admitted, one run; the operator who set 3 expecting three units of concurrency got one). \\u0060DaemonOptions.MaxConcurrentTaskRuns\\u0060 replaces \\u0060MaxConcurrentAgentSessions\\u0060 as the node\\u0027s own admission unit (\\u0060h9k config set --max-concurrent-task-runs\\u0060, \\u0060NodeLoad\\u0060 claims directly in runs now \\u2014 \\u0060Capacity = max(0, MaxConcurrentRuns - LiveRuns)\\u0060, no session-to-run division left in it); the old key is still read as a fallback, converted \\u0060floor(sessions/2)\\u0060 (minimum 1, 2 being the two review lenses\\u0027 peak), independently at each precedence level (\\u0060OperatingSettingsResolver.ResolveMaxConcurrentTaskRuns\\u0060 computes each level\\u0027s own answer \\u2014 new key, else converted legacy \\u2014 before applying the ordinary env-then-file-then-default precedence across levels, so an environment variable naming only the legacy key still outranks a config-file value for the new key), with \\u0060h9k daemon status\\u0060/\\u0060h9k config show\\u0060 naming the conversion when it applies. A second, independent knob, \\u0060DaemonOptions.SessionCapPerRun\\u0060 (global default 3, Brian\\u0027s ruling), caps how many agent sessions one run may hold simultaneously; a per-task override (\\u0060TaskSessionCapOverridden\\u0060, \\u0060h9k task set-session-cap\\u0060) is deliberately state-agnostic \\u2014 unlike \\u0060TaskRevised\\u0060, which is Draft-only, this event applies \\u0022even mid-run\\u0022 and \\u0060ReviewEngine\\u0060 re-reads the effective cap (\\u0060TaskDetails.SessionCap ?? SessionCapPerRun\\u0060) fresh at each dispatch decision rather than once per run, so a change takes effect at the run\\u0027s very next session dispatch: raising it lets the next phase fan out wider, lowering it never terminates a session already running. \\u0060runs=1\\u0060 plus \\u0060cap=1\\u0060 is therefore a strict-serial maximum-throttle mode, and the total possible live sessions on a node (\\u0060runs \\u00D7 cap\\u0060) is emergent rather than configured. Concurrency within a run stays bounded by coded capability, not agent request (the daemon only ever spawns sessions for activities it has coded dispatch logic for \\u2014 today exactly the two review lenses \\u2014 so effective concurrency is 2 by construction regardless of the cap\\u0027s own number, and a cap above 2 is inert headroom until a future coded activity actually overlaps a third session): \\u0060ReviewEngine.DispatchReviewPassesAsync\\u0060 dispatches only \\u0060lenses.Take(sessionCap)\\u0060 up front, and \\u0060DispatchMissingPassesAsync\\u0060\\u0027s own crash-recovery top-up is now budgeted by \\u0060sessionCap - InFlightReviewPasses.Count\\u0060 rather than dispatching every missing lens unconditionally \\u2014 at cap 1 this means the second lens is not spawned until the first lens\\u0027s own \\u0060ReviewPassCompleted\\u0060 has already landed on the stream (proven by \\u0060ReviewEngineTests\\u0060\\u0027 own event-order assertions), which throttles the burn RATE, not the total tokens spent, since the identical two passes still run either way; at today\\u0027s default (3, above the routine peak of 2) both lenses still dispatch together, so nothing about today\\u0027s behavior changes until an operator deliberately lowers the cap. The old whole-life 2-session reservation this replaced (\\u0060NodeLoad.PeakAgentSessionsPerRun\\u0060, Decisions Log #64) dissolves as a concept from the admission side entirely; the constant survives only inside \\u0060OperatingSettings.ConvertLegacyMaxConcurrentAgentSessions\\u0060, computed independently from \\u0060ReviewLens.CycleLenses.Count\\u0060 since Domain cannot reference the Daemon type that used to own it. Every operator-facing surface is run-denominated end to end: \\u0060h9k status\\u0060\\u0027s \\u0022waiting for a slot \\u2014 N of M running\\u0022 line and its queued-section explainer speak in runs with no session arithmetic left in the wording, and an interactive claim (\\u0060h9k task work\\u0060) continues to occupy zero runs \\u2014 structurally, via the \\u0060Guid.Empty\\u0060 \\u0060NodeId\\u0060 sentinel \\u0060NodeLoad.LiveSlots\\u0060 already excluded, unchanged by this decision \\u2014 with the setting help text on both \\u0060h9k config set --max-concurrent-task-runs\\u0060 and \\u0060h9k task set-session-cap\\u0060 stating the rule. This task ships no project-level surface: the per-project ceiling belongs entirely to a later task built on the \\u0060max-concurrent-task-runs\\u0060 denomination this one establishes. **Does this block the later vision?** No: a re-denomination of one existing setting into two, a new state-agnostic task event with the same generation-fence machinery \\u0060TaskClaimed\\u0060 already relies on, and a budget-aware version of dispatch logic \\u0060ReviewEngine\\u0060 already had \\u2014 no change to the review loop\\u0027s own findings/verdict/settlement model.\u0022,\u0022OriginIncident\u0022:null,\u0022Supersedes\u0022:[],\u0022Provenance\u0022:{\u0022RecordedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022RunId\u0022:null,\u0022TaskId\u0022:null,\u0022Attendance\u0022:\u0022Unobserved\u0022,\u0022IsFromRun\u0022:false},\u0022RecordedAt\u0022:\u00222026-09-22T13:15:38.803749\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022LegacyId\u0022:\u0022Decisions Log #111\u0022}","originEventId":"2ca2abd4-0161-4fb5-801b-9ee7a2fab864","originSequence":58911,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-09-22T13:15:39.710965+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"},{"streamId":"01a0c941-fb35-74c4-88e2-6773ffc1c628","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Decision.DecisionRecorded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0c941-fb35-74c4-88e2-6773ffc1c628\u0022,\u0022Scope\u0022:\u0022Project\u0022,\u0022ScopeId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Statement\u0022:\u0022**The three per-run review-cycle caps (\\u0060MaxComplianceReviewCycles\\u0060, \\u0060MaxAdversarialReviewCycles\\u0060, \\u0060MaxFinalFullPassRounds\\u0060) become settable at three levels \\u2014 node, project, task \\u2014 strictly \\u0060task \\u003E project \\u003E node \\u003E compiled default\\u0060, resolved independently per cap; a fourth setting, the task-lifetime review-cycle budget (default 25), counts cycles across every run and follow-up a task has had and is immune to the per-run resets those give the other three** (Brian\\u0027s ruling, 2026-08-29, hardened 2026-08-30 after task b6dfcbe5 reached 52 review cycles across nine generations: every per-run cap fired correctly and repeatedly, but every new run \\u2014 a stranding salvage, a retry, a follow-up round \\u2014 reset the per-run counters, so no cap ever saw the task\\u0027s true history). This entry originally claimed number #108, then #109, then #111, on the assumption that at most one competing branch would land first; the concurrency-configuration branch (decision #111 above) landed first, and its own doc comments went through the identical collision and retitling, so this entry takes #112 instead. Node: \\u0060h9k config set --max-compliance-review-cycles/--max-adversarial-review-cycles/--max-final-full-pass-rounds/--lifetime-review-cycle-budget\\u0060, durable in \\u0060config.json\\u0060 (\\u0060OperatingSettings\\u0060, mirrored into \\u0060DaemonOptions\\u0060\\u0027 own compiled defaults so the two never drift), reported by \\u0060h9k config show\\u0060/\\u0060h9k daemon status\\u0060 through the existing \\u0060OperatingSettingsResolver\\u0060/\\u0060OperatingSettingsRendering\\u0060 machinery (#82). Project: \\u0060h9k project set\\u0060 with the same four options, \\u0060\\u0027default\\u0027\\u0060 clearing the override \\u2014 \\u0060ProjectSettingsChanged\\u0060 carries each as \\u0060Optional\\u003Cint?\\u003E\\u0060, the same present-with-null-clears idiom \\u0060TaskRevised.EpicId\\u0060 (#100) already uses. Task: a new \\u0060h9k task set-review-caps \\u003CID\\u003E\\u0060 command and \\u0060TaskReviewCapsOverridden\\u0060 event, deliberately state-agnostic like decision #111\\u0027s own \\u0060TaskSessionCapOverridden\\u0060 precedent \\u2014 settable at any time, including against a Claimed task whose run is live, so a human can hand a grinding task back to themselves with no new state or command: setting a cap at or below the cycles that track has run since its last human takeover grant (0, if it has never had one, which is also when this count matches the absolute review cycle number \\u0060h9k status\\u0060/\\u0060h9k task show\\u0060 print \\u2014 a grant or a track reactivation moves this count\\u0027s own base forward, and only from there do the two numbers diverge) parks the run the next time that cap is actually consulted \\u2014 a per-track cap at its next fix-session dispatch, the final-full-pass cap at its next mandatory round (the takeover lever) \\u2014 but does not stop a run that converges clean before reaching one of those checks; the lifetime budget is the one exception, checked at every settle point. \\u0060ReviewCapResolver\\u0060 (\\u0060Hall9k.Daemon.Review\\u0060) is the first strict hierarchy walker for an int setting in this codebase \\u2014 \\u0060ReviewRerequestPolicy.Resolve\\u0060 (#62) and \\u0060DaemonOptions.ResolveModel\\u0060 (#33) are the nearest precedents, but neither is strictly ordered this way (the model chain puts the node\\u0027s per-role default above the project). \\u0060ReviewTrackPolicy.CapReached\\u0060/\\u0060CapFor\\u0060 take a \\u0060ResolvedReviewCaps\\u0060 instead of a raw \\u0060DaemonOptions\\u0060; \\u0060ReviewEngine.DriveAsync\\u0060 resolves it fresh every loop iteration \\u2014 not once per \\u0060ReviewAsync\\u0060 call the way \\u0060ReviewContext\\u0060 is \\u2014 the same discipline \\u0060VerifyCommandsFingerprintMatchesAsync\\u0060 already uses for a project setting that can change mid-run, since a review pass or fix session can run for real wall-clock hours. The lifetime budget needed no second counter: \\u0060ReviewEngine.LifetimeReviewCycleCountAsync\\u0060 sums each of a task\\u0027s other runs\\u0027 own \\u0060RunDetails.ReviewCycle\\u0060 (its per-run high-water mark) plus the current run\\u0027s own \\u0060RunAggregate.ReviewCycle\\u0060, at every settle point, immune to \\u0060ReviewParkResolved\\u0060\\u0027s existing \\u0060ReviewBudgetBaseCycle\\u0060/\\u0060FinalFullPassRounds\\u0060 resets by construction \\u2014 it is never reset by anything. Its release reuses \\u0060RunAggregate.HumanEndedTheLoop\\u0060 rather than inventing a new grant: \\u0060ParkIfLifetimeBudgetExceededAsync\\u0060 skips the check outright when \\u0060MaySettleReason\\u0060 returns \\u0060SettleReason.Human\\u0060 (a fresh \\u0060h9k review resolve --merge-ready\\u0060), so a human\\u0027s own verdict for THIS settle proceeds even with the budget spent, while every automatic settle \\u2014 \\u0060Bar\\u0060 or \\u0060NothingOwed\\u0060, even a fully clean one \\u2014 still parks once the budget is exceeded, exactly matching \\u0022every subsequent settle point parks for a human until a human resolution.\\u0022 Every park message this task\\u0027s caps can trip (\\u0060CapParkReason\\u0060, \\u0060FinalFullPassCapParkReason\\u0060, the new \\u0060LifetimeBudgetParkReason\\u0060) now names the resolved value and which of the four levels (\\u0060ReviewCapLevel\\u0060: \\u0060Task\\u0060/\\u0060Project\\u0060/\\u0060Node\\u0060/\\u0060Default\\u0060) supplied it \\u2014 \\u0060Node\\u0060 and \\u0060Default\\u0060 are told apart by comparing the node\\u0027s resolved value to the compiled default, a cosmetic gap only (an explicit node config equal to the compiled default reads as \\u0060Default\\u0060) since it never changes which value is enforced. A general task-pause state was considered and rejected: the blast radius across the dispatcher, \\u0060h9k status\\u0060, and closeout surfaces outweighed the need once these four settings exist. **Does this block the later vision?** No: additive settings and one new state-agnostic task event, reusing the existing node/project settings-change surfaces (#33, #62, #82) and the existing human-override plumbing (#22, #63, #92, #101) rather than inventing new (2026-09-01, origin: three fix-round strandings a same-session hunt would have caught before they cost a full extra verify-plus-fix lap \\u2014 cea5ae6e cycle 6 landed a reflog fix on only one of two branch-creating arms that needed it, b6dfcbe5\\u0027s park found a two-escape cancellation finding with only one escape closed, and cea5ae6e cycle 8\\u0027s hurried reflog re-fix silently swapped prompt\\u0027s \\u0060## Resolution\\u0060 line: a mandatory class sweep, per finding actually fixed, enumerates every other site sharing that defect\\u0027s shape from \\u0060git diff clearing each one inside the branch\\u0027s own changes, and merely naming, not fixing, a pre-existing site outside them, unless this cycle\\u0027s own findings document separately dispositions that exact sibling as a finding of its own (an explicit disposition always wins, regardless of which finding\\u0027s sweep surfaced the sibling) or the finding whose sweep surfaced it is itself dispositioned \\u0060FixHereInItsOwnCommit\\u0060 (in which case an undispositioned sibling is fixed in that same separate commit too \\u2014 both keys coexist, restoring the carve-out this
